products.title: Dinamic Oil RE Slewing Gearboxes — 4,350 to 163,500 Nm, Pinion Output
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil RE slewing gearboxes: 14 frame sizes, nominal output torque 4,350 to 163,500 Nm, pinion or splined output, static brakes for open or closed circuits. Built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
RE slewing gearboxes are Dinamic Oil's planetary drives for slewing rings: an RE gearset on a reinforced output support that carries the radial load of the pinion meshing with the ring gear. Fourteen frame sizes, RE 240 to RE 8010, cover nominal output torques up to 4,350 Nm on the smallest frame and 163,500 Nm on the largest, in two or three stages, for mobile, offshore and deck cranes, aerial platforms, excavators, concrete pumps, container gantries and azimuth thrusters.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Ratings

The table gives each size's nominal output torque T2 FEM — Dinamic Oil's figure for F.E.M. class M5 (L2-T5) at 15 rpm output, an indicative value confirmed per application — and the ratio range for each number of stages. The output support has its own static and dynamic torque limits in the catalogue: the lower of the support limit and the gearset's T2max governs, and the static limit must never be exceeded.

Supports, shafts and pinions

Each size comes with one or more output supports, listed in the table by Dinamic Oil's support code — the eccentric ones (marked ecc) let the pinion-to-ring backlash be set — and a choice of splined or cylindrical output shaft or a pinion. The table lists the supports and the catalogue's pinion range for each size (module and number of teeth); pinions are splined on, or cut integral with the shaft, and pinions outside the catalogue are made to the ring-gear data you send.

Approvals

ABS product design assessments 22-2218009-1-PDA and 25-0346164-PDA cover specific RE and RA 810, 1020 and 1520 builds with pinion output for azimuth-thruster steering, valid to February 2027 and November 2030. Design approval by DNV, ABS, RINA, Bureau Veritas, Lloyd's Register or CCS is available on demand for other builds.

Inputs, brakes and lubrication

Inputs for hydraulic (orbital or axial piston) and electric motors are the same as Dinamic Oil's planetary gearbox range. Static negative brakes come in a low-opening-pressure version for closed-loop circuits and a dry version for high-speed motors. Oil or grease lubrication is available; standard ambient range up to +40 °C.

faqs.question: What do I need to send for a quotation?
faqs.answer: Send the application, the output torque (or line pull) it must deliver, the output or cable speed, the motor you will drive it with, the mounting and output you need, and any class approval the job calls for. Dinamic Oil confirms the order code against that, and we quote with the delivery time from the factory in Italy.

faqs.question: What is T2 FEM?
faqs.answer: The nominal output torque for F.E.M. mechanism class M5 (load spectrum L2, utilisation T5) at 15 rpm output. It is an indicative rating: for a different class, speed or duty, Dinamic Oil checks the selection case by case.

faqs.question: Can the pinion backlash be adjusted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dinamic Oil offers eccentric output supports (marked ecc in the table) that let the pinion-to-ring backlash be set on assembly; the other supports are fixed.

faqs.question: Which brake should I choose?
faqs.answer: On a closed-loop (hydrostatic) slewing circuit, the low-opening-pressure static brake, which releases from the charge pressure. With a high-speed hydraulic or electric motor, the dry brake version.

faqs.question: Can they run in Gulf summer temperatures?
faqs.answer: Dinamic Oil rates its standard units for an ambient temperature up to +40 °C. Above that, or in continuous duty in direct sun, tell us the actual operating temperature so the lubricant and duty can be checked with the factory.

faqs.question: Are these genuine Dinamic Oil units?
faqs.answer: Yes. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, and every unit is supplied new, direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Modena, with the manufacturer's documentation.

products.title: Dinamic Oil GB Heavy-Duty Slewing Gearboxes — 195,000 to 460,000 Nm
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil GB slewing gearboxes: 4 frame sizes, nominal output torque 195,000 to 460,000 Nm, pinion or splined output, static brakes for open or closed circuits. Built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
The GB slewing gearboxes extend the slewing range above the RE sizes: four frames, GB 12010 to GB 26000, with nominal output torques up to 460,000 Nm in three or four stages, for large offshore and deck cranes, harbour and dockyard cranes and tunnel boring machines. Dinamic Oil builds slewing solutions to order up to about 2,000,000 Nm.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Ratings

The table gives each size's nominal output torque T2 FEM — Dinamic Oil's figure for F.E.M. class M5 (L2-T5) at 15 rpm output, an indicative value confirmed per application — and the ratio range for each number of stages. The output support has its own static and dynamic torque limits in the catalogue: the lower of the support limit and the gearset's T2max governs, and the static limit must never be exceeded.

Supports and pinions

Supports, shafts and pinions for the GB sizes are not tabulated in the catalogue — they are designed with the order. Send the slewing-ring data (module, number of teeth, profile shift, face width), the radial load and the mounting space, and Dinamic Oil's technical department sizes the output.

Selection

Size the drive on the slewing torque — the ring's friction, wind and inertia loads, divided by the ring-to-pinion ratio and the number of drives on the ring — then check it against T2 FEM for the duty class, and the start-up and braking peaks against the output support's dynamic limit. Large rings often use two or more drives sharing the load.

Approvals

Design approval by DNV, ABS, RINA, Bureau Veritas, Lloyd's Register or CCS is available on demand.

Inputs, brakes and lubrication

Inputs for hydraulic (orbital or axial piston) and electric motors are the same as Dinamic Oil's planetary gearbox range. Static negative brakes come in a low-opening-pressure version for closed-loop circuits and a dry version for high-speed motors. Oil or grease lubrication is available; standard ambient range up to +40 °C.

products.title: Dinamic Oil GR Wheel Drives with Integrated Orbital Motor — 470 to 1,600 Nm
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil GR 80 and GR 200 wheel drives: planetary hub with built-in orbital motor, 16 motor variants, 470–1,600 Nm continuous, up to 2,500 Nm peak. Built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
GR wheel drives combine a single-ratio planetary gearbox with an orbital hydraulic motor in one compact hub: the wheel bolts to the output flange and the unit bolts to the chassis. Two sizes — GR 80 (ratio 5.23) and GR 200 (ratio 6.2) — each come with a choice of motor displacement, giving continuous output torques of 470 to 1,600 Nm and peak torques up to 2,500 Nm. They are built for light self-propelled machines such as scissor and boom lifts, small loaders, AGVs and vineyard straddle robots.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Range

The table lists each motor variant with its total displacement (motor displacement times the gearbox ratio), continuous and peak output torque, maximum output speed and oil flow. The motor's pressure drop for each torque rating and the flange and port dimensions are in Dinamic Oil's wheel and track drive catalogue.

Options

A mechanical release can be fitted so the vehicle can be towed with the drive disengaged.

Selection

Size the drive on the tractive effort at the wheel: rolling resistance plus gradient times the machine weight on that wheel, times the wheel's rolling radius, gives the torque. Check it against the continuous rating for normal travel and the peak rating for starting on a slope, and the wheel speed against the maximum output speed.

Lubrication and service

Dinamic Oil gearboxes run in an oil bath of EP gear oil, ISO VG 220 to 320; fill before start-up and recheck the level after a few minutes' running. Change the oil after the first 150 operating hours, then at the interval in the use and maintenance manual or at least every two years. Synthetic oil is recommended for very high ambient temperatures. The manual is attached to this page.

products.title: Dinamic Oil EH and EW Planetary Wheel Drives — 3,950 to 24,000 Nm
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil EH and EW planetary wheel drives for hydraulic or electric motors: 6 frames, 3,950 to 24,000 Nm, 2 or 3 stages, 48/96 V DC electric versions. Built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
EH and EW wheel drives are planetary gearboxes for a hydraulic or electric motor, with a wheel flange on the rotating housing and bearings that carry the machine's weight on that wheel — up to 8,000 kg on the EH models. Six frames cover maximum output torques from 3,950 Nm (EH 210) to 24,000 Nm (EW 2500), for skid-steer loaders, scissor and boom lifts, container AGVs and other self-propelled machines; their bearing capacity also suits track drives.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Range

The table lists every two- and three-stage build with its ratio or ratios, the frame's maximum output torque T2max and the weight. EH frames come in S, SC and PD output versions; the EW range has a single version. Flange, spigot and bolt dimensions are in Dinamic Oil's wheel and track drive catalogue.

Electric versions

EHe and EWe versions carry a permanent-magnet synchronous (PMSM) electric motor for 48 V DC or 96 V DC battery machines, with a built-in negative electric brake, so a battery machine needs no hydraulic circuit for travel. Other voltages and executions are made on request.

Options

The EW range has a mechanical release as standard so the vehicle can be towed; on the EH it is an option. Hydraulic versions take orbital or axial piston motors; brakes and control valves are available as accessories.

Lubrication and service

Dinamic Oil gearboxes run in an oil bath of EP gear oil, ISO VG 220 to 320; fill before start-up and recheck the level after a few minutes' running. Change the oil after the first 150 operating hours, then at the interval in the use and maintenance manual or at least every two years. Synthetic oil is recommended for very high ambient temperatures. The manual is attached to this page.

products.title: Dinamic Oil T Series Hydraulic Towing and Recovery Winches — 2,700 to 30,000 daN
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil T series hydraulic towing and recovery winches: 7 sizes, 2,700 to 30,000 daN first-layer pull, 10 to 26 mm cable, drum freewheel and multi-disc brake. Built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
Dinamic Oil's T series are hydraulic pulling winches for tow trucks, recovery vehicles, lorries, agricultural and forestry machines and any job that needs a horizontal pull. Seven sizes give first-layer line pulls from 2,700 daN (T27 IN) to 30,000 daN (T300) on 10 to 26 mm cable. The design keeps the hydraulic motor, the static brake and the planetary gearbox as separate modules on the drum, which makes installation and maintenance simpler.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Construction

  • Orbit hydraulic motor with a pilot-operated overcentre valve mounted on it, which stops the load running back.
  • Negative static multi-disc brake, closed by disc springs and released by the motor pressure.
  • Drum freewheel — manual, pneumatic or hydraulic — so the cable can be pulled out by hand to the vehicle.
  • Cast iron or steel drum on high-capacity bearings, planetary gearbox in an oil bath, cast or fabricated frame.

Options

Cable tensioner (B), fairlead cable guide (C2) or both (C1); four rotation and cable-exit arrangements (counterclockwise or clockwise, cable over or under the drum). Dinamic Oil recommends 6x36 Warrington Seale IWRC cable to ISO 2408, 2,160 N/mm², in 10 to 26 mm.

Use

The table gives the first-layer pull, cable speed, cable, motor, flow, pulling pressure, ratio, brake torque and weight; the datasheet gives four layers in SI and imperial units. Keep at least five wraps of cable on the drum and the return-line back pressure under 5 bar. These are pulling winches: they must not be used to lift or carry people.

Sizing

Choose the winch on the pull it must deliver on the layer it will work from — the first layer gives the highest pull and the lowest speed. A snatch block on the casualty roughly doubles the available pull at half the cable speed, less the sheave's losses. Check that the truck's hydraulic pump delivers the winch's oil flow at its pulling pressure.
